title: Oracle-Assisted Factoring of Almost All Inputs
statement: With the specified elliptic-curve point-count-multiple oracle, Theorem 1.2 deterministically finds a nontrivial factor for almost all inputs in the bounded population.

target.description: Inputs $n\le X$ outside an exceptional set of size at most $X/(\log X)^\delta$ for sufficiently large X; X renames the source's upper bound N to distinguish it from an individual input.

parameters.name: X
parameters.meaning: Upper bound on the input population (source N)

auxiliary_information: MultEll(X,B,M) of Definition 1.1 supplies bounded positive multiples of E(n,b), the product of point counts over prime factors, for eligible b; it may reject nonsquarefree inputs.

time.note: Theorem 1.2's classical algorithm bound; it does not include a cheap implementation of the oracle. Section 1.5 discusses the separate oracle-computation cost.

memory.note: No memory bound is established in this selected extraction.

oracle_calls.note: Query accounting of Theorem 1.2; not coherent access to a secret-key oracle.

success.description: The deterministic theorem gives an exceptional-set size bound over the population n<=X, not a randomized success probability for a specified RSA integer. The density guarantee stays in the target and statement.

review.scope: Checked Theorem 1.2, the exceptional-input handling and Algorithm 3.1. No per-input randomized success is stated.

evidence.locator: PDF/printed pp. 5–7, Definition 1.1, Theorem 1.2, Remark 1.5 and oracle-cost discussion; pp. 13–14, Algorithm 3.1.
evidence.interpretation: Targeted primary-text transcription; no full-paper audit, global frontier certification or independent implementation run.

limitations: The exceptional set includes cases not handled by the stated oracle/preselection model; no guarantee for every RSA modulus follows.
The one-query oracle of Theorem 1.4 is a different model and is not mixed into this configuration.
